title: The Caliph Omar bin al-Khattab and the Young Badawi
summary: In the reign of the Caliph Omar bin al-Khattab, two young brothers brought a handsome young Bedouin before the council in Medina, saying:...
keywords: the caliph omar bin al-khattab and the young badawi
full_text:
In the reign of the Caliph Omar bin al-Khattab, two young brothers brought a handsome young Bedouin before the council in Medina, saying: 'O Commander of the Faithful, this man’s camel entered our orchard and destroyed our fruit trees. When our father threw a stone at the camel, this youth struck back in anger, and our father perished. We demand justice according to the law.'

The young Bedouin stood tall, with clear, untroubled eyes, and confessed: 'It is true, O Caliph. The stone our father threw killed my prize mare; in my youthful anger, I struck him with my staff, and his spirit departed. I do not deny the deed, and I submit to the law. But I have one prayer: my father died leaving a great treasure of gold entrusted to me for my younger orphan brother, buried in a secret place in the desert. Grant me a reprieve of three days, that I may dig up the gold, place it in the hands of a guardian, and return to face judgment.'

Omar asked: 'Who among this assembly will stand as your surety with his own life if you fail to return?'

The youth looked around the hall, but he was a stranger, and no man knew him. Suddenly, Abu Dharr al-Ghifari, the venerable companion of the Prophet, stood forward and said: 'I will stand as his surety, O Caliph.'

The court was filled with awe; if the stranger did not return, the revered Abu Dharr would face execution!

Two days passed, and the third day arrived. As the sun began to sink toward the horizon, the youth had not appeared. The crowd began to weep for Abu Dharr.

Just as the sun touched the rim of the desert, a lone figure appeared running across the sands, covered in dust and drenched in sweat! It was the young Bedouin. He fell exhausted at Omar’s feet, gasping: 'I have secured my brother’s inheritance! Here is my life; execute your law!'

Omar wept and asked: 'Why did you return, when you could have fled into the vast desert where none could find you?'

The youth answered: 'I returned so that no man should ever say: "Honor and faith have vanished from among men!"'

Omar turned to Abu Dharr: 'And why did you vouch for a stranger?' Abu Dharr replied: 'So that no man should say: "Trust and brotherhood have perished from the world!"'

The two brothers, weeping in profound realization, stepped forward and said: 'We forgive him! We remit his blood-debt freely, so that no man should ever say: "Mercy and forgiveness have died in the human heart!"' The entire assembly cheered in joy, celebrating the triumph of honor.
moral: Keeping one's sacred word in the face of death inspires universal mercy and reconciles enemies.
